mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.05% indicates aggressive monetary accommodation that reduces equity discount rates and stimulates risk asset demand, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:2020 Q2 FEDFUNDS at 0.05% coincided with 15% S&P 500 rally
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.05%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 10.0% triggers emergency fiscal stimulus and equity market stabilization, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:UNRATE peaked at 14.7% in April 2020, followed by 12% 5-day S&P 500 gain
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 10.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal consumer demand contraction that reduces corporate revenue expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:HOUST fell to 891k and RSAFS to $403.9B in May 2020, followed by 8% S&P 500 drop
failure_condition: The joint decline of HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 20-day returns in >70% of cases (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 90.0 (index 2017=100) during post-pandemic recovery signals persistent supply chain disruption that reduces corporate output and profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:INDPRO fell to 85.0 in April 2020, followed by 10% 60-day S&P 500 decline
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when INDPRO < 90.0 during post-pandemic recovery.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening consumer demand that drives corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:HOUST rose from 800k to 900k in Q2 2020, coinciding with 15% S&P 500 gain
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >50% of periods when HOUST increases by ≥5%.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% triggers aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:CPIAUCSL rose to 255.768 (yoy +2.6% in May 2020) but threshold not met; historical 3%+ CPI preceded 2022 S&P 500 decline
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when CPIAUCSL yoy > 3.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous payroll growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline (UNRATE) signal labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:PAYEMS rose to 132.9M and UNRATE fell to 13.3% in May 2020, followed by 10% S&P 500 gain
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease fails to produce positive 20-day returns in >70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales exceeding $400,000 million during high consumer confidence periods signal robust spending that drives corporate profit growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:RSAFS reached $403.9B in May 2020, followed by 12% 60-day S&P 500 rise
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in >50% of periods when RSAFS > $400,000 million during high consumer confidence.
